author_or_institution: Charles A. Czeisler and colleagues (consensus report authors)
title: Catastrophes Sleep and Public Policy: A Consensus Report
book_use: Establishes the recurring pattern of major industrial disasters clustering at circadian low points and shift-work fatigue as a contributing factor. Connective source for the disaster-timing pattern in Chapter 1, developed further in Chapters 8-12. Published in Sleep journal.

title: Backgrounder on the Three Mile Island Accident
book_use: Confirms the Three Mile Island accident began at 4:00 a.m. on March 28 1979, and shift workers failed to recognize loss of coolant between 4 and 6 a.m. Official source for the accident timeline; also cited in Chapter 9.

title: Chernobyl Time-line April 1986
book_use: Establishes that the Chernobyl test began at 1:23 a.m. on April 26 1986 and that a less-experienced night shift took over mid-test. Also cited in Chapter 8.

title: The Catastrophe and After
book_use: Independent secondary account of the Chernobyl disaster sequence and aftermath, written shortly after the events, corroborating the chronology.

title: Bunker Experiment
source_type: Tertiary summary of a documented research program
book_use: Describes the 1964-1989 Andechs bunker experiments led by Aschoff and Wever, the isolation protocol, and scale (418 studies, 447 subjects). Used only for uncontroversial procedural and scale facts; interpretive claims are sourced separately to Czeisler 1999.

title: Circadian Timing
book_use: First-person account by the researcher who led the Andechs bunker program, published in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences.

title: Stability Precision and Near-24-Hour Period of the Human Circadian Pacemaker
book_use: Refines the human intrinsic circadian period to 24.18 (+/- 0.04) hours using forced-desynchrony protocols, correcting the earlier roughly-25-hour bunker-era estimate. Central refinement source distinguishing early free-running estimates from later, controlled measurement. Science 284, 2177-2181.

author_or_institution: The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet
title: The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine: Advanced Information
book_use: Documents the award to Jeffrey Hall, Michael Rosbash, and Michael Young for discovering molecular mechanisms controlling circadian rhythm, including the 1984 isolation of the period gene and the transcription-translation feedback loop.

title: Rosbash Awarded 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
book_use: Institutional account of Rosbash's role isolating and characterizing the period gene at Brandeis University, used for biographical and institutional detail.

title: Suprachiasmatic Nucleus
book_use: Confirms that lesion studies by Moore and Eichler and by Stephan and Zucker independently identified the suprachiasmatic nucleus as the master circadian pacemaker in 1972.

title: Molecular Architecture of the Mammalian Circadian Clock
book_use: Establishes that peripheral tissue clocks (liver, muscle, heart, and others) are self-sustained and cell-autonomous but require synchronization by the SCN, with only 1-3% overlap in oscillating transcripts between tissues.

author_or_institution: Till Roenneberg, Tim Kantermann, Myriam Juda, Martha Merrow
title: Social Jetlag: Misalignment of Biological and Social Time
book_use: Coins the term social jetlag, defined as the discrepancy between social and biological time, drawing on the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire dataset of more than 25000 participants. Foundational source for the chronotype chapter.

author_or_institution: Neda Ghotbi, Andrea Rabenstein, Luisa K. Pilz, Tobias Ruther, Till Roenneberg
title: Chronotype Social Jetlag and Nicotine Use
book_use: Later empirical study linking late chronotype and social jetlag to smoking prevalence, used as a dated example of chronotype research beyond the original 2006 coinage.

author_or_institution: Dustin M. Graham, Kwoon Y. Wong
title: Melanopsin-Expressing Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cells
book_use: Explains the discovery of melanopsin and ipRGCs as a third retinal photoreceptor system, motivated by circadian light responses persisting in mice and humans lacking functional rods and cones.

title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder in the Blind
book_use: Documents that Non-24 sleep-wake disorder occurs in 55-70% of totally blind individuals because loss of light perception removes circadian entrainment, with melatonin-based treatment described. Natural-experiment evidence for how essential the photic entrainment channel is.

author_or_institution: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
title: FastStats: Sleep in Adults
book_use: Reports that 30.5% of U.S. adults surveyed in 2024 slept fewer than the recommended seven hours per night, with only about half waking feeling well-rested most days. Primary statistical source for the scale of insufficient sleep.

author_or_institution: RAND Corporation (Marco Hafner, Martin Stepanek, Jirka Taylor, Wendy M. Troxel, Christian van Stolk)
title: Why Sleep Matters: Quantifying the Economic Costs of Insufficient Sleep
book_use: Estimates the U.S. economy loses up to $411 billion a year (2.28% of GDP) to insufficient sleep, with comparative figures for the UK, Canada, Germany, and Japan. Central economic-cost source for the sleep-debt chapter.

title: Is Matthew Walker's Why We Sleep Riddled with Scientific and Factual Errors
source_type: Academic blog analysis of a published critique
book_use: Documents specific factual and statistical errors identified in Matthew Walker's popular book Why We Sleep, including a misleadingly altered chart, and the university inquiry that found no formal misconduct. Used as a cautionary case study on popular sleep science outrunning its evidence, not as a source for sleep-science facts.

author_or_institution: Rutgers University (Thomas A. Edison Papers Project)
title: Life of Thomas Alva Edison and Companies
book_use: Documents Edison's 1863-1869 night-shift telegraphy work, the 1881 Newark lamp factory, and the 1882 Pearl Street commercial electric light station in Manhattan. Institutional archive source for the history of electric light enabling continuous industrial operation.

title: Ford and Edison in a Modern Regulatory Environment: The First-in-Human Trial of Night-Work and Artificial Light
book_use: Frames Edison's introduction of electric light as, in effect, mass unregulated human experimentation with night work and artificial light exposure, adopted before its physiological costs were understood.

title: Chernobyl Disaster
book_use: Provides consolidated timeline and casualty detail for the April 26 1986 disaster, corroborating the 1:23 a.m. test start and night-shift staffing already sourced to ch01-chernobyl-timeline-laka and ch01-holloway-catastrophe-after; used only for uncontroversial chronology and casualty facts.

title: How Fatigue Played a Role in Some of the World's Biggest Disasters
book_use: States that Chernobyl investigators attributed operator fatigue, following 13-hour shifts, as a leading contributor to the human error behind the explosion. Industry-safety synthesis, flagged in prose as distinct from a formal accident-investigation finding.

title: Circadian Rhythms and Shift Work
book_use: States that the hours between 3 and 5 a.m. are a period of lowest alertness and cites a 30% increase in human-error incidents on night shift relative to morning shift; discussed alongside the Three Mile Island case.

title: The World's Deadliest Industrial Disaster Exposed 500000 People to Toxic Gas
book_use: Documents that the Bhopal leak was discovered around 11:30 p.m. on December 2 1984, with catastrophic release after midnight, and that halving the night-shift operator count left the plant severely under-resourced. Primary journalistic account of the Bhopal timeline and night-shift staffing.

title: The Bhopal Chemical Gas Disaster
book_use: Historical account of the understaffing, substandard safety procedures, and dismissive initial response by the night-shift supervisor at the Union Carbide plant, corroborating staffing and decision-making detail.

title: Joseph Hazelwood Exxon Valdez Captain in 1989 Alaska Spill Dies at 75
book_use: Confirms third mate Gregory Cousins was on watch, fatigued after covering for an exhausted colleague, when the Exxon Valdez ran aground on Bligh Reef at 12:04 a.m. on March 24 1989. Primary journalistic source for the timeline and crew-fatigue detail.

title: The Complete Story of the Exxon Valdez Oil Spill
book_use: Details the National Transportation Safety Board finding that crew fatigue and the third mate's failure to make a scheduled turn contributed to the grounding.

author_or_institution: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce Science and Transportation
title: Aviation Safety: One Year After the Crash of Flight 3407
book_use: Official congressional record of the February 12 2009 Colgan Air Flight 3407 crash near Buffalo New York and the fatigue and commuting concerns it raised.

title: Colgan Air Flight 3407 Crash: NTSB Findings Pilot Training Issues and Aviation Litigation
source_type: Legal and engineering analysis of NTSB findings
book_use: Summarizes the NTSB probable-cause finding centered on crew response to the stick shaker, the extensive pilot-commuting patterns at Colgan Air (about 20% of pilots commuting over 1000 miles), and the board's decision to raise fatigue as a contributing concern without naming it a causal factor. Preserves the contributing-versus-causal distinction as counter-evidence against an overstated fatigue narrative.

title: Clarification of Flight Duty and Rest Requirements (14 CFR Part 117)
book_use: Documents the FAA's January 2012 final rule overhauling pilot flight duty and rest requirements, enacted after the 2010 Airline Safety and FAA Extension Act directed science-based reform following Flight 3407.

author_or_institution: International Agency for Research on Cancer (summarized by ISGlobal)
title: IARC Retains Probably Carcinogenic Classification for Night Shift Work
source_type: Research institute summary of an official classification
book_use: Documents IARC's 2007 classification of shift work involving circadian disruption as a Group 2A probable human carcinogen, reaffirmed in 2019, based on limited human evidence and adequate animal evidence.

title: Attributing the Burden of Cancer at Work: Three Areas of Concern When Examining the Example of Shift-Work
book_use: Raises confounding (self-reported schedules, smoking, diet) and the limits of epidemiological evidence behind the shift-work cancer classification. Central counter-evidence source preserving the scientific debate about causality.

title: A Case That Shook Medicine
book_use: Documents the October 1984 death of 18-year-old Libby Zion at New York Hospital under the care of overworked, under-supervised medical residents, and her father's subsequent campaign for reform.

title: The Evolution of Residents Hours
book_use: Traces the path from the Bell Commission's recommended 80-hour resident workweek, adopted by New York State in 1989, to the ACGME's 2003 national 80-hour standard.

title: Nursing Performance Medication Error and Patient Safety Concerning Night Shift Rotations
book_use: Reports that night-shift medication errors were far more likely to result in harm (74%) than day-shift errors (18%), and that most medication errors (65.8%) occurred during night shift. Central quantitative source for the night-shift nursing error data.

title: How Jet Lag Hurts Diplomats Without Them Even Realizing It
book_use: Recounts Secretary of State John Foster Dulles's jet-lagged 1956 negotiation over Aswan Dam financing, followed by the surprise announcement that Egypt had purchased Soviet weapons, as a historical illustration of travel fatigue affecting high-stakes decisions.

title: How Jet Lag Impairs Major League Baseball Performance
book_use: Uses 20 years of MLB data to show jet lag measurably and specifically affects skills including pitching and base running, at times erasing home-field advantage. Primary quantitative sports-science source for jet lag's performance effects.

title: Eastward Jet Lag Is Associated with Impaired Performance and Game Outcome in the National Basketball Association
book_use: Finds eastward travel associated with impaired NBA home-game performance after adjusting for covariates, consistent with jet-lag mechanisms. Corroborates direction-dependent jet lag effects across leagues.

title: The Time for Chronotherapy in Radiation Oncology
book_use: Reviews evidence that toxicity and efficacy of several anticancer drugs vary by more than 50% depending on time of administration, with specific timing improving outcomes for cisplatin, 5-fluorouracil, and doxorubicin combinations.

title: Why Does Circadian Timing of Administration Matter for Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors Efficacy
book_use: Summarizes retrospective evidence that early-in-day infusion of immune checkpoint inhibitors was associated with up to fourfold better progression-free or overall survival compared with late-day infusion.

author_or_institution: Cheri D. Mah, Kenneth E. Mah, Eric J. Kezirian, William C. Dement
title: The Effects of Sleep Extension on the Athletic Performance of Collegiate Basketball Players
book_use: Documents that Stanford men's basketball players who extended nightly sleep by an average of 110.9 minutes improved sprint time from 16.2 to 15.5 seconds and shooting accuracy by 9%, with better mood and reaction time. Primary study for the athletic-performance chapter.

title: School Start Times for Adolescents
book_use: Recommends that middle and high schools start no earlier than 8:30 a.m., citing adolescent circadian phase delay as a key modifiable contributor to insufficient teen sleep. Primary policy-statement source for the school-start-time chapter.

author_or_institution: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
title: Sleep and Health (Healthy Schools)
book_use: CDC guidance endorsing later school start times to address adolescent sleep insufficiency and circadian misalignment.

author_or_institution: Christopher Kyba and colleagues (summarized for the public)
title: Light Pollution Can Suppress Melatonin Production in Humans and Animals
source_type: Peer-reviewed research summarized for the public
book_use: Reports illuminance thresholds at which artificial light at night suppresses melatonin (as low as 6 lux in sensitive humans, lower for blue-shifted light), and links nighttime light exposure to sleep, metabolic, and mood disruption.

title: Artificial Light at Night: Melatonin as a Mediator Between the Environment and Epigenome
book_use: Reviews mechanisms by which artificial light at night disturbs nocturnal melatonin production and downstream health associations, including epidemiological co-distribution with breast cancer incidence.

title: How Crypto Traders Navigate Volatility and Mental Health
book_use: Documents burnout patterns specific to 24/7/365 cryptocurrency markets, including survey findings that 88% of traders check prices more than 40 times daily and 71% experience sleep disturbance tied to market volatility.

title: Collaborating Across Time Zones: Digital Platforms Asynchronous Practices and Performance in Global Virtual Teams
book_use: Finds that effective collaboration in low-time-zone-overlap teams depends on documentation and asynchronous practices rather than default synchronous communication, and that real-time communication effectiveness declines with each hour of time difference.
